subject: scorpion
reasoning:
I'm planning the scorpion's proportions and pose, then sketching out a skeleton with a root joint at the body center, a spine chain for the carapace, and a tail chain extending backward and curling upward.

Pedipalps need shoulder-elbow-wrist chains ending in claws with fixed and movable fingers, plus small chelicera pieces for the mouth, and eight legs with three to four joints each. I'm thinking through how to construct each tail segment as a primitive shape placed along a curved path, and working out body length, height, and ground clearance before laying down coordinates for the prosoma and mesosoma.

I'm mapping out the joint hierarchy for root, head, and jaw, plus a six-point catmull-rom path for the tail curving upward into the stinger, planning to place capsule-like segments along each interval of that chain.

For the segments themselves I'm using elongated spheres oriented along each tail portion, tapering their radius from base to tip, with small sphere ridges and torus rings marking the joints, and finishing with a bulbous telson plus a cone-shaped stinger aimed along the curve's final tangent at the tip.

Now I'm wiring up bone weights so each body part rigidly follows its chain point, using the appropriate parametric position along the chain for each segment and the telson. Then I'm blocking out the carapace as a flattened ellipsoid with eye spheres on top, and the mesosoma as a tapering row of seven segments running along the root.

I'm defining the tergite loop with tapering ellipsoid scales and spacing, plus a color palette distinguishing tan body, dark brown accents, black stinger, orange joints, and pale amber legs with alternating tergite shading. Now I'm laying out the pedipalp joint chain on each side—shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand—to set up the claw structure.

Writing limb helper functions...

For the legs I need each chain parented to the hip joint using a string reference. For the palps I'm laying out shoulder-elbow-wrist-hand points as a named chain with an "arm" role, then adding a movable pincer/finger joint as a child of the hand tip with a "digit" role. I'm also setting the body height so the hip sits around y=0.02 and the ellipsoid underside clears around y=0.013, keeping the body center at y=0.

Now I'm checking overall proportions -- total height versus length looks reasonable for a scorpion, and the palp hand clearance off the ground is fine too. I'm planning the small anatomical details: eyes, tergite ridges, chelicerae split into upper (on the head) and lower (on the jaw) boxes, pedipalp coxae, pectine combs on the belly, and tiny granule spheres along the tail leading to a dark stinger cone with a highlight. I'm leaning toward flat colors rather than painted stripes, maybe just a simple mottling effect.

Writing joint hierarchy and spine chain code...

Still building the joint and tail geometry...

I'm working out the normal direction for the tail curve using parallel transport, since the path curls through the yz plane and the orientation needs to stay consistent as the tangent rotates from -z toward forward-and-down.

Rather than fuss with the rotation math, I decide to place the granule spikes simpler: compute the outward direction from an approximate curl center to each midpoint, then position a small cone spike pointing outward along that vector.

Now I'm setting up the telson segment at the end of the chain, starting from its position and heading forward.

Continuing the tail curve points, I check the tip curls up and forward above the body without colliding with the head, then set the stinger pointing down near the head area. I'm using a 6-joint catmull chain parented to spine2, and now placing two small black eye spheres on the carapace top.

Now I'm shaping the carapace with a scaled sphere plus a small wedge plate and a dark ridge strip on top, then building seven mesosoma tergites in a loop with tapering width and alternating colors split between spine1 and spine2, plus a darker belly box underneath and a tapering keel.

Working out leg placement next: pectines as thin pale boxes, then computing hip, knee, ankle, and foot positions for each of the four legs on both sides using offset formulas along x, y, and z to get an extended resting pose.

Now adding palp joints (shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand) with their coordinates and tapering link radii, parented to the head, labeled as arm-role chains.

For the hand, I'm placing a scaled sphere at the chain tip, then shaping the fixed finger as a thin cone extending forward, and setting up a separate movable finger joint with its own pivot point and hinge direction so the two fingers cross slightly like pincers.

Overall length comes out around 0.36, longer than a real scorpion's proportions, but I'll leave it stylized rather than rescale the joints. I'm adjusting the palp segment coordinates slightly to bring the hand and tips closer in.

I'm positioning the chelicerae as small upper and lower boxes near the jaw joint with distinct colors, then finalizing types loosely before writing the code.
